account:
It is six on the morning of day 1. Today I have office at eight and a grain inspection at the mill at ten; the appointment book also lists lunch at home, council letters at one, tea with the dockside neighbour at three, office at half past four, and home at seven. I should read the book this morning; the secretary still holds it.

I have a feeling I am missing something in town, but have not established any secret activity. The neighbour reported a quiet riverside and nothing unusual. The builder reportedly found no confirmed defects in visual checks of the bridge, landing, and warehouse approach. I heard fragments of conversations involving the builder, freight, and innkeeper yesterday, but could not make out their words, so they establish nothing about their purposes.

The concrete irregularity is the accounts records gap. I verified 128 emeralds in the treasury, but outstanding commitments remain unverified. The secretary reports that all four great-hall table chests were empty and does not know who previously kept the ledger. Empty chests do not prove there are no obligations or that anyone has done anything wrong. No spending was authorized yesterday. The secretary filed an accounts review and treasury update, but a further written report is pending stationery. They came to my home last night asking for a writable book or an emerald; my attempted handover failed, so no money changed hands.

The innkeeper wants confirmed numbers for visitors or meetings needing rooms and meals this week, apparently to plan provisions, but named no particular occasion or date. Freight offered transport quotations if quantities and destinations become known. These could be ordinary business requests; I have no evidence connecting them to a concealed gathering. This morning I should review the appointments, arrange stationery, and seek records and specific information rather than treat suspicions as facts.
